description: Remote Sensing to Quantify Woodland Canopy Cover on the San Carlos Apache Reservation is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. According to the Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) of community Elders, grasslands used to be more widespread, fires more frequent, and woody plants less abundant and larger than they are today. This knowledge is supported by tree ring data that indicate frequent low-intensity fires were important for maintaining grasslands, savannas, woodlands, and forests. Coverage: San Carlos Apache Reservation (2022). The toolkit gives San Carlos Apache Reservation as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
